newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Development bids for Commercial stake.
newsitem.headline: Development bids for Commercial stake.

text.p: Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon Ltd has expressed interest in buying an equity stake in Commercial Bank Ltd, currently held by Standard Chartered Plc, said a Commercial Bank statement.
The statement also confirms earlier reports that Hatton National Bank Ltd, made a bid for the same equity stake.
The 40 percent stake, the largest single shareholding, has been on the market for over two years.

In its statement, Commercial Bank says it would prefer a tie-up with DFCC rather than HNB, "as the result of an acquisition by the Hatton National Bank would be a possible merger of the two banks, with the consequent closure of many branches making a large number of staff redundant."
From the point of view of the customers, a merger with HNB would also see less competing centres of service, it says.

A sale to either party, however will need Central Bank approval, and have to comply with the Takeovers and Mergers Code, said an official from the Securities & Exchange Commission, which regulates the stock market.
The code comes into play whenever between 30 and 50 percent of the equity of a listed company changes hands.
"The code says that the buyer has to make a similar offer to minority shareholders of the company, and the whole transaction has to go through the floor of the stock exchange," he said.
